config.title: Conditional Rendering with Ternary

intro.title: Conditional Rendering with Ternary
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that displays a dynamic message based on a condition. You will learn how to use the ternary operator for conditional rendering directly in your template. The main technologies involved are Vue's template syntax and JavaScript's ternary operator. This approach allows you to show or hide content efficiently with a concise, inline expression. By the end, you'll be able to control UI elements based on state changes in a clean, readable way.
intro.usecase: Conditional rendering with ternary operators is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to user context. In e-commerce sites, you'll see this pattern when showing 'Add to Cart' vs 'Out of Stock' buttons based on inventory status. Dashboard applications use it to toggle between 'Loading...' spinners and data visualizations when fetching completes. Form validations frequently employ ternary operators to display error messages only when input fails checks, keeping interfaces clean until needed.

objectives: Implement a ternary expression within a Vue template to conditionally render text content
Apply a ternary operator to control the display of HTML elements based on component state
Construct a Vue component that uses ternary logic to toggle between two different UI structures
Bind a ternary expression to element attributes for dynamic styling or behavior
Manipulate component data properties to trigger different conditional rendering outcomes
Integrate ternary-based conditional rendering with user interaction handlers
Configure a Vue template that uses multiple ternary expressions for complex display logic
Render different components or template fragments using ternary operators in the template section

steps.title: Add template structure with conditional rendering
steps.instruction: In the template, add a div that uses a ternary operator to display 'Welcome back!' when isLoggedIn is true, otherwise display 'Please log in'.
steps.hint: Use the ternary operator inside double curly braces in the template. The syntax is {{ condition ? expressionIfTrue : expressionIfFalse }}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of ternary in Vue template
{{ isVisible ? 'Visible!' : 'Hidden' }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a div that conditionally renders text based on the isLoggedIn state using a ternary operator.
successCriteria: The template includes a div with a ternary operator that displays 'Welcome back!' when isLoggedIn is true and 'Please log in' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your div uses the ternary operator correctly with isLoggedIn and displays the appropriate messages.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required conditional rendering. Add a div with a ternary operator that checks isLoggedIn and displays the correct messages.

steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Toggle Login' inside the template, and wire its click event to call the toggleLogin function.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to attach the toggleLogin handler to the button's click event.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Toggle Login' appears below the conditional text, and clicking it toggles the message between 'Welcome back!' and 'Please log in'.
successCriteria: The template contains a button element with the text 'Toggle Login' and an @click directive that calls the toggleLogin function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and the @click handler is properly wired to toggleLogin.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not correctly connected. Add a button with text 'Toggle Login' and set its @click to toggleLogin.

steps.title: Add conditional styling with ternary
steps.instruction: Add a class binding to the message div that uses a ternary operator to apply the 'logged-in' class when isLoggedIn is true, otherwise apply the 'logged-out' class.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can bind classes dynamically with :class. Use the ternary operator to conditionally assign class names based on isLoggedIn.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The message div will have dynamic styling: when isLoggedIn is true, it gets the 'logged-in' class; when false, it gets the 'logged-out' class.
successCriteria: The div element has a :class binding that uses a ternary operator to assign 'logged-in' or 'logged-out' based on isLoggedIn.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the :class binding uses a ternary operator with isLoggedIn to switch between 'logged-in' and 'logged-out'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The class binding is missing or incorrect. Use :class with a ternary operator to apply 'logged-in' when isLoggedIn is true and 'logged-out' when false.

steps.expectedOutcome: A span element appears in the UI that shows ✓ when logged in and ✗ when logged out.
